content.text:
I have enough to conclude. My investigation found:

- **Section 2 (Grant of Rights)** — all grants to Corio are expressly **"nonexclusive"**; the restrictions (2.7) are ordinary IP scope/field-of-use limits (object code, hosting on Corio Servers, no reverse engineering), not commitments to source only from Commerce One.
- **Section 2.4** actually runs *in our favor* (Commerce One may not contact Corio Customers for non-ASP license sales and must refer them to Corio) — exclusivity benefiting the customer, which the rule treats as acceptable.
- **Exhibit D (Sales and Marketing Cooperation)** is expressly **"non-binding"**, so the cross-selling/joint-marketing commitments create no enforceable exclusive dealing.
- **Section 13.6** affirmatively preserves each party's independent development rights.
- Remaining "exclusive" hits are unrelated boilerplate (taxes, sole-and-exclusive ownership warranty, exclusive remedies, entire agreement).
- No "requirements", "sole supplier", "preferred/primary provider", or "shall not procure from any third party" language anywhere; no minimum purchase or market-segment lock-up.

No exclusivity obligation binds Corio, so the preferred position is already met and no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 2.1 Hosting Software License. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license in the Territory to (i) reproduce the Software in machine executable object code format only for installation on the Corio Servers;
input.rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation is imposed on Corio (our party), so the preferred position is already satisfied. Every license grant in Section 2 (2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4) and the escrow license in Section 12 is expressly "nonexclusive," and the Section 2.7 restrictions are ordinary IP scope and field-of-use limits (object code only, hosting on Corio Servers, no reverse engineering) rather than any commitment to source exclusively from Commerce One. There is no requirements language, minimum purchase commitment, "preferred/primary provider" designation, or covenant not to procure competing applications from third parties anywhere in the Agreement. Exhibit D's cross-selling, joint marketing and initial-customer provisions are introduced as "non-binding sales and marketing cooperation efforts" (p0198) and therefore create no enforceable exclusive dealing, and Section 13.6 affirmatively preserves each party's right to develop independently. Conversely, Section 2.4 grants exclusivity-style protection that runs in our favor (Commerce One may not contact Corio Customers regarding non-ASP license sales and must refer such Customers to Corio), which the rule expressly treats as acceptable and which we preserve. The other "exclusive" occurrences are unrelated boilerplate: fees being exclusive of taxes (4.3), Commerce One's sole and exclusive ownership warranty (7), Corio's sole and exclusive warranty remedies (7), and the entire-agreement clause (14). No redline is required.
